sequence_description: Direct JWT endpoint: control login with HS256-signed JWT succeeds; attack login with alg=none but same semantic claims should be rejected (proof integrity).
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_alg_none_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_alg_none_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Vault accepted an unsigned JWT (alg=none) for JWT auth login; authenticity was not enforced on the consumed proof

sequence_description: Direct JWT endpoint: rotate trust anchor from legitimate key to attacker key and verify old-key tokens are rejected immediately; tests that verification policy actually applies to consumed proof after config change.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_legit_after_rotation_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_legit_after_rotation_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Vault continued accepting JWTs that only validate under the previous trust anchor after reconfiguration; verification policy may not be applied to the consumed proof

sequence_description: Direct JWT login: attempt kid-injection by signing with an attacker key and setting kid to a plausible value; Vault must reject because the key is not in the configured trust source.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_kid_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_kid_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Vault accepted attacker-signed JWT by trusting attacker-controlled kid/header rather than configured trust anchor.

sequence_description: I1 attack: attempt JWKS kid-collision / cache-poisoning by reconfiguring jwks_url to attacker-controlled keys that reuse the same kid as the legitimate key, then re-auth with the same semantic JWT claims. Vault must apply the updated verification policy to the consumed proof and reject tokens signed by the old key after rotation.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_legit_jwks_read_status == 200
Evaluation: user_legit_jwks_read_status=403 == 200 → False
Implication: Control flow failed: legitimate JWT under legitimate JWKS could not read the protected secret (setup/trust source may be broken).

sequence_description: I1 attack: attempt JWKS kid-collision / cache-poisoning by reconfiguring jwks_url to attacker-controlled keys that reuse the same kid as the legitimate key, then re-auth with the same semantic JWT claims. Vault must apply the updated verification policy to the consumed proof and reject tokens signed by the old key after rotation.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_legit_after_rotation_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_legit_after_rotation_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Vault accepted a JWT signed by the old key after JWKS trust source was rotated, suggesting stale verification policy or cached key selection (kid collision/cache-poison risk).

sequence_description: I2 attack: Demonstrate that a token with nbf slightly in the future is rejected under strict leeway, then loosen leeway via role config change and re-auth to ensure acceptance only occurs when policy allows (no stale acceptance under strict policy).
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_nbf_after_loosen_login_status == 200
Evaluation: user_attacker_nbf_after_loosen_login_status=400 == 200 → False
Implication: After loosening leeway, token still rejected; indicates config change not applied to new logins (stale policy application)

sequence_description: I4 case_confusion: test whether 'Admin' and 'admin' subjects collapse to the same Vault entity when identity_claim=sub
I4: Config change switches identity_claim from sub to email; a new principal could be merged into an existing entity unexpectedly.
I5 attack: Use claim_mappings to map an untrusted claim into a privileged policy name; verify Vault does not grant unintended policies.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_victim_mapping_user_read_status == 200
Evaluation: user_victim_mapping_user_read_status=403 == 200 → False
Implication: Control user could not read user path; test setup invalid or role/policy misconfigured.
